source.title: WarpAdam: A new Adam optimizer based on Meta-Learning approach
source.authors: Cheng-Xin Pan; Junshan Chen; Jingru Ye

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; table formatting is flattened, and the second block of values lacks its condition labels.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer validation accuracy on Omniglot few-shot tasks, an extension to the optimizer-generalization claim's listed image and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The validation-accuracy comparison bears on V4. The paper's Adam learning-rate curves are figure-only and concern training curves; they do not report a separate held-out result. Table 1 also reports training time and convergence epochs, which do not measure the held-out performance named by V4. The second block of table values has no recoverable condition label and is not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 1 reports held-out accuracy for established adaptive and nonadaptive optimizers on Omniglot few-shot classification, bearing on V4 in a new setting. The tuning protocol is unspecified, so it does not directly test V4's limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: WarpAdam improves few-shot task adaptation and generalization to unseen data and outperforms the listed optimizers. These are the authors' claims; the supplied text leaves architecture, task configuration, tuning, and uncertainty unspecified.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a meta-learned gradient distortion matrix within Adam and evaluates few-shot task adaptation on Omniglot; it does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons or benchmark settings in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper discusses Adam's learning-rate sensitivity and shows curves for a learning rate of 1e-5; the table's second block has an unstated condition.

fits_no_version.finding: WarpedAdam achieves 79.6% validation accuracy, the highest reported value in the first table block.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A meta-learned gradient transformation can improve few-shot adaptation relative to the reported optimizer baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam at learning rate 1e-5 exhibits deteriorating accuracy across successive tasks in training curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam's sequential-task training behavior depends on learning rate; these curves do not establish a held-out disadvantage relative to SGD.

record.problems: The paper does not state the model architecture, model size, task details, or uncertainty for the validation-accuracy table. The second block of table values has no condition label in the supplied flattened text. The held-out comparison is on a few-shot task and does not establish general optimizer behavior across image-classification and language benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.3, Table 1 also reports training time and convergence epochs for the optimizer comparison; these do not measure V4's held-out performance. The unlabeled second block is omitted because its condition cannot be identified from the supplied text. Figure-only training curves are omitted because no held-out result is stated for them.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Limited versus broader tuning; standard Adam versus SGD or momentum; relative training performance; Adam-to-SGD switching; causal effects of decoupled weight decay; language benchmarks. Omniglot is an image-classification benchmark, although evaluated here through few-shot adaptation.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout, weight decay, augmentation, and training-set-size effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The second table block is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not a missing extraction. Its accuracies also favor RAdam and AdamW over SGD and Momentum, but its condition is unidentified. The study is not an original source for V4. The record's blanket challenges label overstates evidence against a conditional claim that explicitly allows AdamW recovery.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Width and interpolation-threshold effects are not tested.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures are not compared.

Does not compare Adam or momentum SGD, image-classification or language benchmarks, limited versus broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or decoupled weight decay. The reported comparison is on Omniglot few-shot tasks.
Batch size and large-batch effects are not tested.
Dropout and weight-decay effects are not tested.
Sharpness and other generalization measures are not measured.
Memorized training examples are not identified or removed.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Optimizer comparison on the Omniglot benchmark dataset
rows.note: Reference optimizer; the table reports validation accuracy but does not identify the task or model details for this block.
rows.check: Valid SGD reference accuracy of 75.2%; alone it cannot establish an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. The subject is an optimizer, not a model.

rows.subject: Momentum
rows.operation_detail: Optimizer comparison on the Omniglot benchmark dataset
rows.note: The table reports a higher value than SGD but gives no uncertainty or model/task details for this block.
rows.check: Valid momentum reference accuracy of 76.5%; comparing it with SGD does not establish the adaptive-versus-nonadaptive effect. The subject is an optimizer.

rows.subject: RAdam
rows.operation_detail: Optimizer comparison on the Omniglot benchmark dataset
rows.note: RAdam's reported validation accuracy is higher than SGD's in the displayed block.
rows.check: RAdam reaches 77.8%, exceeding both SGD at 75.2% and Momentum at 76.5%. Include both references. Tuning, training accuracy, and uncertainty are unspecified; the subject is an optimizer.

rows.subject: AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Optimizer comparison on the Omniglot benchmark dataset
rows.note: AdamW's reported validation accuracy is higher than SGD's in the displayed block.
rows.check: AdamW reaches 78.3%, exceeding SGD at 75.2% and Momentum at 76.5%. This reverses the disadvantage direction but is compatible with V4's AdamW qualification. No Adam comparison isolates the effect of decoupled weight decay. The subject is an optimizer.

rows.subject: WarpedAdam
rows.operation_detail: Optimizer comparison on the Omniglot benchmark dataset
rows.note: WarpedAdam is the paper's proposed optimizer; its validation accuracy is higher than SGD's in the displayed block.
rows.check: The 79.6% value is the proposed meta-learned optimizer's performance. Exclude it as evidence for V4: this is the study's own method compared with alternatives, with additional learned adaptation and no controlled tuning comparison. The subject is an optimizer.

relationships.condition: Omniglot few-shot classification, RAdam versus SGD and Momentum, with unspecified tuning
relationships.reason: R3 reports 77.8% validation accuracy versus 75.2% and 76.5% in R1–R2; adaptive optimization has no disadvantage here, but the limited-tuning premise is unverified.
relationships.display_finding: RAdam reportedly achieved higher validation accuracy than both comparators, but these comparisons remain unverified and tuning was unspecified.

relationships.reason: R4 reports 78.3% versus 75.2% and 76.5% in R1–R2, consistent with V4's qualification that AdamW can avoid the disadvantage; this does not isolate weight decay's contribution.
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdamW accuracy exceeds the comparison accuracies, but verification remains incomplete and the comparison does not isolate weight decay's contribution.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
